clues.title: Google car: Gen4 low cam
text: All the Gen4 coverage taken in Sri Lanka is low-cam(gen3 coverage in Sri Lanka is not low cam), the only two other countries with low-cam is Japan and Switzerland but they look different. You can recognize lowcam because of wide blur of the street view car and lower vantage point compared to normal camera.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Unique car
text: In most Generation 3 Sri Lanka coverage, you will be able to see the front of the Google car partially through the blur. It appears as blue-white-red patches, reminiscent of the French flag, with the red patch usually being the most visually distinct.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Rural roads often have outside lines, but no middle lines.
In the absence of other clues, this can sometimes be a way to decide a tough 50-50.
**NOTE:** Most small roads lack road lines entirely.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Horton Plains National Park
text: Horton Plains National Park has a very distinct and bait landscape, consisting of hilly plains covered in long grass. In the distance, you can see forests, but most of the park’s roads meander through a wide open landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Drier Climate
text: Conversely, the rest of the country has a slightly more dry climate. The vegetation is often lower and more open. The landscape usually has a mix of brown and green tones.
Note that the difference is not extreme, as the landscape in Sri Lanka never truly gets downright arid.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Southern Climate
text: The southwest of Sri Lanka has a more wet climate that is characterised by lush, dense vegetation. Deep green tones dominate the landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 Lowcam
text: All Generation 4 coverage is low-cam.
**This can be recognized in two ways:**
The car blur is significantly bigger.
Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.
Sri Lanka’s Generation 3 coverage is made with a normal height camera!

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Shitcam
text: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Sri Lanka.
This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.
Within Asia, India and Cambodia also have shitcam coverage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: concrete square pole
text: Square poles with small pinholes in the sides. These pinholes are limited to the top part of the pole.
NOTE: The square poles with small pinholes can look very similar to those found in Thailand. However, in Thailand the pinholes extend all the way to the bottom of the pole.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: concrete holey pole
text: Poles with large see-through holes in the lower half of the pole (“holey poles“). These poles are unique to Sri Lanka.

clues.title: Sri Lanka
text: Sri Lankan telephone numbers have 10 digits.
The first three digits of landline phone numbers are the area code. The first digit of that area code is always a 0, while the remaining two digits are shown on the map.
Mobile phone numbers always start with 07 and are not associated with any particular region.
Image credit: Maccem.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Pole
text: Sri Lanka typically uses concrete utility poles. Two pole types are common and distinctive:
Square poles with small pinholes in the sides. These pinholes are limited to the top part of the pole.
Poles with large see-through holes in the lower half of the pole (“holey poles“). These poles are unique to Sri Lanka.
They also commonly have those 3 big insulators on top of the pole shown on the second image.
**NOTE:** The square poles with small pinholes can look very similar to those found in Thailand. However, in Thailand the pinholes extend all the way to the bottom of the pole.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
